content.comment_body: I'm using the astroclock function to lower my roller shutter at sunset. However, when I try to open it in the morning before sunrise, it closes again because the system still treats this as a sunset event. Is it possible to keep using the astroclock and open the roller shutter in the morning without it automatically closing?
You can add a NAND (with edge detection) block between the astroclock and the OR block. Please see the attached image for reference.
Thanks for your prompt response. I've already implemented your suggestion and will test it tonight when the shutter is down. I feel confident that this will solve the issue. Thanks.
When the astronomical clock switches off, the NAND (with edge detection) block sends out a pulse for one cycle. To generate another pulse, the astroclock needs to switch on again and then switch off.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced a problem where controlling roller shutters with the astroclock caused the shutter to close again in the morning when the intent was to open it before sunrise. The thread highlights that the system doesn't clearly distinguish between sunrise and sunset in its event logic, leading to confusion when setting up automated actions. Users appreciated a fast workaround suggestion but brought to light a challenge in customizing event-based automation using the astroclock.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the astroclock feature to both close the shutter at sunset and reliably allow it to open in the morning before sunrise without being triggered to close again. The product should differentiate clearly between sunrise and sunset scenarios so that automations work as intended.
